newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called little changed amid firm cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called little changed amid firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open unchanged to slightly higher Wednesday following a calm ACCESS session and early talk of steady cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.12 to $2.135 after settling to the downside Tuesday at $2.122 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 0.8 cent higher at $2.13.
At the Henry Hub, cash prices were talked flat to one cent higher at $2.15-2.18 per mmBtu.
"I think they'll try to penetrate that $2.11-2.12 level to test $2.08-2.10," one trader said.

Creating some downward pressure in the market may be the forecasts calling for cooler weather over the Northeast, Midwest and Southwest over the weekend and into early next week, Weather Services Corp reported.
In the near-term, above-normal temperatures are expected to continue in the Northeast through Friday.
Resistance in July was seen first at $2.21, then at $2.25, $2.37 and the contract high at $2.44.
Early injection estimates for today's weekly AGA storage report range from 85 bcf to 110 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 88 bcf.

In Tuesday's cash, swing gas in the Louisiana Gulf slipped a couple of cents to the mid-teens. Midcontinent pipes were down a similar amount to about $2.00-2.02. New York city gate gas was a few cents lower in the low-$2.40s.
